With two-and-a-half weeks to go until Mississauga election day, talk about potentially redeveloping a notable chunk of the city’s downtown entered into the campaign on Thursday as mayoral candidates put forward various policy ideas and focuses. While unveiling the remaining parts of her campaign platform, Bonnie Crombie said she wants to put a stop to studying the potential demolition of the Living Arts Centre as part of a massive redevelopment project. 5-billion vanity project at a time when residents are struggling with everyday bills; this is the wrong priority,” she told reporters, arguing any potential municipal funding should be redirected to other priorities and initiatives. The Living Arts Centre, located just north of Mississauga city hall and west of Square One, opened in 1997. It has a 1,300-seat main auditorium along with various meeting rooms and exhibition spaces.

items.title: SIU Clears Peel Police in Death of Man Who Fell From Mississauga Balcony This Summer
items.summary: According to the Special Investigations Unit, the provincial watchdog has closed its investigation into the death of a man who fell from the balcony of a Mississauga condo this past summer, finding police had no chance to save him. The SIU said Peel officers were dispatched to a building on Kingsbridge Garden Circle, near Highway 403, after a woman called police on July 29 to report her boyfriend had assaulted her. The SIU said officers knocked on the unit's door, identified themselves and called out the man's name, but got no answer. According to the SIU's account, the 34-year-old man placed a chair near the balcony railing and was seen climbing onto it. The agency said an officer moved toward the sliding glass door and called out for the man to stop, but he fell before officers could reach him. The SIU is automatically called in whenever a death or serious injury occurs during an interaction between police and the public, and its investigation concluded officers were not at fault in this case.

items.title: Ward 7 Candidate Jerry Krzywda Says Affordability and Safe Streets Drove Him to Run
items.summary: According to Modern Mississauga Media, Ward 7 council candidate Jerry Krzywda says he's running because his family has deep roots in the ward, where he's now raising his own children after his family immigrated from Poland when he was six. Krzywda told the outlet he spent part of his childhood in Cooksville and considers Ward 7 home. He said he wants the ward to be a place where residents, whether renting or owning, can afford to live and build a future, where seniors can stay in the communities they know, and where people can count on safe streets, well-maintained public spaces and dependable city services. The profile is part of Modern Mississauga Media's 2026 election series, which invited every candidate to answer the same set of questions ahead of the Oct. 26 municipal vote. The outlet said the series aims to boost voter turnout after historically low engagement, noting candidates were asked to submit at least four images alongside their unedited answers. Modern Mississauga Media said it will continue posting candidate profiles as they come in, with each one published within 72 hours of being received.

items.title: Mississauga Reconstructing Two North-End Trails to Add Up to 25 Years of Life
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, the city is reconstructing two popular trails in its north end as part of an effort to extend their service life by up to 25 years. The city said in a project update that the improvements aim to create safer, more accessible connections throughout the surrounding neighbourhood, supporting walking, cycling, recreation and everyday travel. Ward 9 Coun. Martin Reid said residents should expect the ongoing construction to cause temporary trail closures while the work is underway. The city said the reconstructed trails will be built to current municipal standards, providing reliable, low-maintenance infrastructure for the community. Officials said the upgrades are expected to extend the trails' service life by roughly 20 to 25 years while reducing future maintenance needs. The city said it will post advance notice signs to alert residents to any upcoming temporary closures or construction activity that could affect them.

items.title: Where do Mississauga mayoral candidates stand on public safety, police funding?
items.summary: 4 candidates invited to Mississauga Board of Trade debate. Mayoral candidates outline their plans for e-scooter enforce… Candidates outline plans on how they will address the Peel Regional Police funding formula and public safety concerns. Several Mississauga mayoral candidates outline how they will address regional police funding and public safety concerns ahead of the election on Oct. 26 Increasing Peel Regional Police budgets and public safety are two election issues on the minds of voters in the upcoming municipal election. We offered mayoral candidates an opportunity to address those issues. Candidates were asked to respond in 200 words to each of these two questions: What steps will you take to address rising concerns around organized crime, break-ins, and auto theft? How will you ensure residents see results from public safety spending, and what tools will you use for budget accountability? Here’s what they said in email statements. Responses have been edited for length.

items.title: Diwali Celebration and Collectibles Expo to Share Mississauga's Downtown Core This Weekend
items.summary: According to Insauga, two very different events will take place just steps apart in downtown Mississauga from Oct. 9 to 11: Diwali RazzMatazz and Nostalgia Fest Expo. Diwali RazzMatazz returns to Mississauga Celebration Square for three days of Indian culture, music, food and family entertainment, hosted annually since 2014 by the Indo-Canada Arts Council. Organizers told Insauga the festival draws more than 50,000 attendees each year, with Bollywood performances, live musical concerts, cultural dance showcases, a Diwali Bazaar and kids' activities and rides planned for this year's event. Meanwhile, Nostalgia Fest Expo will take over the Square One Event Hall for three days centred on trading cards, collectibles and nostalgia, featuring games like Magic: The Gathering alongside sports cards. Insauga reports the expo will also include toys, action figures, anime merchandise and other nostalgic collectibles, along with special guests and celebrity appearances. Both events land in the same downtown core that's home to the city's main entertainment hub and one of Ontario's busiest shopping centres.

items.title: Mississauga Man Takes $500K Lump Sum After 30 Years of Playing the Lottery Finally Pays Off
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, Dennis Cidade, a 50-year-old Mississauga man who has played the lottery for about 30 years, won his first major prize after scoring the Daily Grand second prize of $25,000 a year for life in the Sept. 3 draw. Rather than take the annuity, Cidade chose a lump-sum payment of $500,000. The winning ticket was purchased at Apple Party Mart on North Service Road. Cidade said he found out he had won after breakfast one morning and could not process the news at first. He told the Ontario Lottery and Gaming Corporation in a news release that the experience felt out of this world. Mississauga.com reports his mother was the first person he told about the win.

items.title: Brampton Power-of-Sale Listings Have Nearly Doubled Mississauga's Total So Far in 2026
items.summary: According to Insauga, the number of power-of-sale property listings in Brampton so far this year is roughly double the total in neighbouring Mississauga, with one real estate analyst warning that more mortgage distress is still to come. A power of sale can happen when a homeowner defaults on their mortgage, allowing the lender to sell the property to recover outstanding debt. Insauga reports Brampton currently has 45 active power-of-sale listings, while Toronto leads the region with 179 active listings on the market right now. Real estate watcher John Flynn posted data from the Matrix multiple listing service on X showing 406 new power-of-sale listings in Brampton so far in 2026, compared with 203 in Mississauga over the same period. Insauga reports the figures point to Brampton absorbing a disproportionate share of the region's mortgage defaults as the broader housing market continues to cool.

items.title: Mississauga and Brampton Hospitals Among 26 Sites Getting $47M Push to Cut ER Wait Times
items.summary: According to Insauga, the Ontario government announced Wednesday it will spend more than $47 million over four years on a new Emergency Department Action Team, or EDAT, that will work directly with 26 hospitals across the province to cut emergency room wait times. Insauga reports Mississauga and Brampton hospitals are among the sites included, specifically William Osler Health System's Brampton Civic Hospital and Etobicoke General Hospital, along with Trillium Health Partners' Credit Valley Hospital and Mississauga Hospital. The province said the initiative responds to emergency departments facing sustained pressure from rising patient volumes, more complex cases and growing demands on the health-care system. EDAT will examine how patients move through emergency departments, from initial assessment and diagnostic testing through to admission or discharge, looking for what's causing delays along the way. The province said the 26 hospitals were chosen based on factors including emergency department volumes and the potential for improvements to benefit the largest number of patients. Insauga reports operational and performance indicators, along with representation across different hospital types and regions, also factored into the selection.

items.title: Mississauga's City Centre Lands Among GTA's Cheapest Neighbourhoods to Buy a Home
items.summary: According to Insauga, real estate platform Wahi's monthly ranking of the Greater Toronto Area's least expensive neighbourhoods placed Mississauga's City Centre among the cheapest places to buy last month, the only Peel Region community on the list. Wahi found City Centre's median sold price was $428,750 in September, with 30 homes selling over an average of about 34 days on the market. Insauga reports North York's Flemington Park topped the overall list with a median price of $383,000, where six homes sold in an average of 26 days, while Etobicoke's Woodbine ranked second at $402,000 with five sales averaging 42 days. Wahi builds its rankings each month using median home sale prices in GTA neighbourhoods with five or more sales. Insauga notes the most expensive neighbourhoods on Wahi's list tended to be older Toronto communities and areas known for large properties, a contrast to the bargains showing up amid the broader market's ongoing slowdown this fall.
